name: fda-modality-1990-2025
title: FDA novel drug approvals and market withdrawals by therapeutic modality, 1990-2025
description: Year-by-year modality classification of 1,246 US novel active substance approvals (1990-2025) plus 45 curated US market withdrawals. NOTE: the approvals series is validated against FDA published counts for 2006-2025 and carries lower confidence for 1990-2005; the withdrawals series is curated and its completeness is not benchmarkable. See docs/.

resources.name: approvals_substance_level
resources.description: One row per novel active substance: identity, approval, modality and how the modality was decided.

fields.name: moiety
fields.description: Normalised active moiety name, uppercase. Salts/hydrates stripped to parent; distinct prodrug esters retained.

fields.name: application_number
fields.description: FDA application number, prefix included (e.g. NDA021436, BLA125057).

fields.name: application_prefix
fields.description: NDA or BLA.

fields.name: approval_year
fields.description: Calendar year of first US approval of this moiety.

fields.name: approval_date
fields.description: FDA submission status date for the approval action (ISO date).

fields.name: brands
fields.description: Pipe-delimited brand name(s) recorded on the application.

fields.name: sponsor
fields.description: Applicant/sponsor as recorded by FDA at the time of the pull.

fields.name: fda_submission_class
fields.description: FDA submission class code description for the original submission (e.g. 'Type 1 - New Molecular Entity').

fields.name: final_class
fields.description: Assigned therapeutic modality. One of: Small molecule, Antibody, ADC, Peptide, Protein/Enzyme, Oligonucleotide, Other.

fields.name: final_basis
fields.description: How the modality was decided: rule engine, ChEMBL concordance, model vote, or a written per-case adjudication.

fields.name: era_confidence
fields.description: Per-row evidential tier, matching the `confidence` column of the aggregate tables.

resources.name: withdrawals_substance_level
resources.description: One row per withdrawal: drug, year, modality, basis, reason, and cross-checks.

fields.name: moiety
fields.description: Normalised active moiety name, uppercase. Salts/hydrates stripped to parent; distinct prodrug esters retained.

fields.name: withdrawal_year
fields.description: Calendar year the product was withdrawn from the US market.

fields.name: final_class
fields.description: Assigned therapeutic modality. One of: Small molecule, Antibody, ADC, Peptide, Protein/Enzyme, Oligonucleotide, Other.

fields.name: withdrawal_basis
fields.description: safety, efficacy, or a combination.

fields.name: withdrawal_reason
fields.description: Short description of the withdrawal trigger.

fields.name: returned
fields.description: True if the drug later returned to the US market.

fields.name: return_note
fields.description: Circumstances of return, where applicable.

fields.name: scope
fields.description: 'moiety-wide' or 'formulation' - whether the whole moiety or only one formulation was withdrawn.

fields.name: scope_note
fields.description: Which formulation, for formulation-scoped withdrawals.

fields.name: pipeline_class
fields.description: Modality independently derived by the approvals pipeline, where the drug survives in Drugs@FDA. Blank if purged.

fields.name: approval_year
fields.description: Calendar year of first US approval of this moiety.

fields.name: modality_crosscheck
fields.description: Whether the hand-assigned modality agreed with `pipeline_class`.

fields.name: chembl_withdrawal_year
fields.description: ChEMBL drug_warning year, where present. First GLOBAL withdrawal, not necessarily US.

resources.name: withdrawal_rate_by_era
resources.description: Withdrawals as a percentage of approvals, by era.

fields.name: approvals
fields.description: Count of novel approvals in the era.

fields.name: withdrawals
fields.description: Count of withdrawal events in the era.

fields.name: withdrawal_rate_pct
fields.description: withdrawals / approvals x 100 for the era. Not a per-drug hazard; see KNOWN_ISSUES.
